items: Set Up Your Repair Fund: Calculate 1-2% of your home's purchase price and commit to saving that amount each year for repairs, knowing that a $400,000 home needs $4,000-$8,000 annually.
Set Up Your Repair Fund: Start your repair fund immediately with whatever amount you can afford—even $100 per month—because starting today matters more than waiting for a perfect number.

Set Up Your Repair Fund: Add an extra 0.5% of home value to your first-year savings on top of the baseline, because deferred maintenance from the previous owner commonly surfaces within months of moving in.

Set Up Your Repair Fund: Record the installation ages of your HVAC, water heater, roof, and sewer line to track their lifespans, because knowing replacement timing prevents you from being blindsided by $5,000-$25,000 bills.

Assess Repair Urgency: Recognize true emergencies that require immediate professional help—gas smell, flooding, no heat in freezing temps, sewage backup, or burning electrical smells—because waiting even hours risks serious harm.
Assess Repair Urgency: For gas smells, leave your house immediately and call the gas company emergency line from outside, because operating any electrical switches inside could trigger an explosion.

Assess Repair Urgency: Call a plumber within one week for water heater failure signs like no hot water, leaking, or rust-colored water, because these units over 10 years old are near the end of their predictable lifespan.

Assess Repair Urgency: Use a bucket and mark water level to track slow leak rates before calling a plumber, because this information helps professionals diagnose the problem faster and more accurately.
Handle Repairs Wisely: Get 2-3 contractor quotes for any non-emergency repair to avoid overpaying, because prices vary significantly and you can make informed decisions with multiple estimates.

Handle Repairs Wisely: Compare replacement versus repair costs for appliances over 10 years old when estimates exceed $500, because new units often make better financial sense than expensive repairs on aging equipment.

Handle Repairs Wisely: Call for emergency service immediately without comparison shopping when facing true emergencies, because the premium $150-$300 after-hours charge is worth avoiding life safety risks.
Handle Repairs Wisely: Address running toilets within one month even though they are not emergencies, because a single running toilet can waste 200-300 gallons of water per day until it is fixed.
